tldr_label: TL;DR: Trump, Xi and Putin plan a joint APEC meeting, the US denies Iran hit its radar, and Democrats flip Mississippi

tldr_bullets.label: APEC
tldr_bullets.body: The White House says Trump, Xi and Putin plan a joint meeting on the sidelines of next week's APEC summit in Shenzhen. China and Russia have not confirmed it. [[TAG:info:unprecedented]]

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: CENTCOM says it shot down two Iranian drones aimed at Bahrain and reported no damage, rejecting the Revolutionary Guards' claim that they destroyed a US radar. [[TAG:warning:claims clash]]

tldr_bullets.label: Senate
tldr_bullets.body: AP called Mississippi for Democrat Scott Colom. Mary Peltola leads in Alaska, the last uncalled Senate race. [[TAG:success:Mississippi flips]]

tldr_bullets.label: Inflation
tldr_bullets.body: October wholesale prices rose 0.3% on the month and 6.5% on the year, the highest annual rate in nearly four years. Markets now see a December Fed hike as likely. [[TAG:danger:6.5% PPI]]

tldr_bullets.label: Germany
tldr_bullets.body: Mercedes-Benz froze new investment at its German plants and is examining closures after labour-cost talks failed. [[TAG:warning:industrial strain]]

sections.title: APEC: A Three-Way Summit
sections.summary: White House plans Trump-Xi-Putin meeting in Shenzhen; Iran and nuclear arms on the agenda

paragraphs.heading: The Plan
paragraphs.body: NBC News and the Boston Globe reported that the White House says Trump, Xi and Putin plan an unprecedented joint meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, which runs November 18 to 19. Neither Beijing nor Moscow has confirmed it. A US official said Trump intends to raise Iran, and nuclear arms reduction is also expected to come up. The official called the meeting a starting point and said no agreements are expected. [[TAG:info:not yet confirmed]]

paragraphs.heading: Trump and Xi
paragraphs.body: According to the reports, Trump and Xi will also hold a one-on-one meeting and a working lunch on Thursday. Brookings noted that it would be their second straight APEC meeting, and that the multilateral setting eases pressure to produce major bilateral outcomes. Elon Musk will reportedly travel with Trump but will not join the three-way meeting. [[TAG:info:Thursday talks]]

sections.sources: NBC News, Boston Globe, MS NOW, Brookings, Politis

sections.title: Iran and Oil
sections.summary: US says it downed two drones with no damage; IEA sees crude surplus but diesel still scarce

paragraphs.heading: Radar Dispute
paragraphs.body: Al-Monitor, the Washington Times and Euronews reported that US Central Command denied the Revolutionary Guards' claim that they destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain. CENTCOM said it shot down two one-way attack drones fired at Bahrain overnight, with no injuries or damage. Iran called the attack retaliation for a US strike on a telecom tower in Sirik. Neither account has been independently verified. Euronews reported that diplomacy mediated by Qatar and Pakistan continues. [[TAG:warning:unverified claims]]

paragraphs.heading: IEA Outlook
paragraphs.body: Quartz and Euronews reported that the IEA's November oil market report finds global supply overtaking demand for the first time since the Iran war began, with output up 2.3 million barrels a day in October to 105.4 million. The IEA said diesel remains the market's biggest concern. European diesel is near $180 a barrel, about 77% above pre-war levels, and the agency plans to speed up emergency stock releases. It warned that attacks on shipping remain the main risk to the recovery. [[TAG:warning:diesel tight]]

sections.title: Ukraine: Swap Ahead, Strikes Continue
sections.summary: Largest prisoner exchange of the war agreed; deadly strikes on both sides

paragraphs.heading: Prisoner Exchange
paragraphs.body: PBS NewsHour and NPR reported that Russia and Ukraine agreed at the Abu Dhabi talks to a large prisoner exchange, which NPR described as the biggest humanitarian release since the full-scale invasion. Russian officials put it at more than a thousand prisoners on each side, to take place within two to three weeks. AP noted that the specifics had not been confirmed by both governments. [[TAG:success:biggest swap]]

paragraphs.heading: Strikes
paragraphs.body: Euronews reported that Russian strikes on Friday killed at least three people and injured more than 20 across Ukraine. Ukrinform said three people, including a child, were killed and 62 injured in Zaporizhzhia region over a day. Euronews also reported that Ukrainian drone strikes killed four people at an industrial site in Samara region and four in Volgograd, according to Russian accounts. [[TAG:danger:strikes continue]]

sections.title: United States: Votes and Prices
sections.summary: Colom wins Mississippi; Peltola leads Alaska; 6.5% wholesale inflation firms up Fed-hike bets

paragraphs.heading: Senate Count
paragraphs.body: Coverage reported that AP called Mississippi's Senate race for Democrat Scott Colom over Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith on Wednesday. The Anchorage Daily News reported that Mary Peltola grew her lead over Sen. Dan Sullivan as thousands more ballots were counted, with about 49.8% of first-choice votes. Ranked-choice tabulation may still be needed. Democracy Docket reported that a Trump administration lawsuit challenges the Alaska race's certification. [[TAG:success:Mississippi flips]]

paragraphs.heading: Wholesale Inflation
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that the producer price index rose 0.3% in October, slightly below forecasts, but the annual rate reached 6.5%, the highest in nearly four years. TokenPost said market-implied odds of a quarter-point Fed hike in December rose to 91%. The Fed's next decision is December 9. [[TAG:danger:hike likely]]

paragraphs.heading: Markets and Nvidia
paragraphs.body: TheStreet and the Washington Post reported that on Friday the Dow edged up 0.10% while the S&P 500 fell 0.40% and the Nasdaq 0.91%. All three still gained on the week. TipRanks and Mediaite reported that Nvidia shares fell further after Reuters reported a third alleged affair involving Jensen Huang, with another Nvidia employee. Nvidia declined to comment. [[TAG:warning:Nvidia earnings Tuesday]]

sections.title: Germany: Mercedes Hits Pause
sections.summary: Carmaker freezes investment at German plants and weighs closures after labour talks fail

paragraphs.heading: Investment Freeze
paragraphs.body: RTE and Automotive News reported that Mercedes-Benz has halted new investment at its German plants after failing to agree on labour-cost cuts with its works council and unions. Board member Britta Seeger said the company must now examine closures more closely, though it wants to avoid them. Production chief Michael Schiebe warned that new models could be built only abroad. [[TAG:danger:closures weighed]]

paragraphs.heading: Cost Squeeze
paragraphs.body: Reports said the move follows a cut to Mercedes's 2026 profit outlook. The company is seeking savings that include lengthening the working week from 35 to at least 38 hours. IG Metall is demanding a 5% pay rise. Analyst Ferdinand Dudenhoeffer called it the German car industry's biggest crisis since its inception. [[TAG:warning:union clash]]

sections.title: Israel and Gaza
sections.summary: Eisenkot prioritizes a Haredi coalition; Gaza deaths continue as mediators demand more aid

paragraphs.heading: Coalition
paragraphs.body: The Times of Israel, citing Channel 12, reported that Eisenkot has decided to prioritize a coalition with the ultra-Orthodox parties over relying on Arab parties. Israel.com reported that he says talks are progressing a week into his mandate, though bloc figures describe the contacts as initial soundings. Shas remains closely aligned with Netanyahu. [[TAG:info:Haredi track]]

paragraphs.heading: Gaza
paragraphs.body: Middle East Monitor, citing Anadolu, reported that Israeli attacks killed six Palestinians and wounded about 20 in Gaza on Friday despite the ceasefire. Palestinian health authorities put the toll since the ceasefire took effect above 1,600. Egypt Today reported that the intelligence chiefs of Egypt, Turkey and Qatar met in Cairo and called for a halt to Israeli violations and more humanitarian aid as winter sets in. Israel and Hamas accuse each other of violating the truce. [[TAG:danger:ceasefire strained]]

sections.title: Around the World
sections.summary: Pope Leo's emotional Chiclayo Mass; Sudan's army claims a West Kordofan town

paragraphs.heading: Chiclayo
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and OSV News reported that Pope Leo XIV celebrated an outdoor Mass near Chiclayo, the Peruvian diocese he led from 2015 to 2023. Crowd estimates range from about 500,000, cited by Vatican News, to one million, cited by America Magazine. Al Jazeera said the visit came a month after the pope's lung cancer surgery. [[TAG:success:homecoming Mass]]

paragraphs.heading: Sudan
paragraphs.body: Radio Tamazuj reported that Sudan's army and allied Joint Force fighters said they recaptured the strategic town of Al-Khuway in West Kordofan after heavy fighting with the Rapid Support Forces, which had not commented. A year after the RSF took El Fasher, Amnesty International has documented killings and torture there. Thousands of people remain missing, according to an allAfrica roundup. [[TAG:danger:war grinds on]]
